description: Covers plant tropisms, the structure and function of neurones, synapses and reflex arcs, the sensory eye, and the endocrine roles of the pancreas, pituitary gland and adrenal glands.

mcq.questionText: The growth response of a plant part towards or away from a stimulus is called:
mcq.explanation: The directional growth response of a plant to a stimulus is tropism. Exam Tip: Tropisms named by stimulus: photo-(light), geo-(gravity), hydro-(water), thigmo-(touch).

mcq.questionText: The growth of a plant shoot towards light is called:
mcq.explanation: Growth towards light (photo-) is positive phototropism. Exam Tip: Shoots show positive phototropism and negative geotropism (grow upward).

mcq.questionText: The growth of a plant root towards the pull of gravity (downward) is called:
mcq.explanation: Roots grow downward, towards gravity, so this is positive geotropism. Exam Tip: Roots show positive geotropism (down) and negative phototropism (away from light).

mcq.questionText: The growth of plant roots towards water is called:
mcq.explanation: Hydro means water, so growing towards it is positive hydrotropism. Exam Tip: Positive hydrotropism helps roots find moisture in the soil.

mcq.questionText: The basic unit of the nervous system, specialised to carry nerve impulses, is called a:
mcq.explanation: This specialised cell that carries nerve impulses is a neurone. Exam Tip: Neurones transmit electrical impulses, while nephrons and alveoli carry out different jobs in the body.

mcq.questionText: The part of a neurone that receives impulses and carries them towards the cell body is called the:
mcq.explanation: Dendrites receive impulses and carry them towards the cell body. Exam Tip: Remember dendrite carries impulses towards the cell body, while the axon carries them away.

mcq.questionText: The long part of a neurone that carries impulses AWAY from the cell body is called the:
mcq.explanation: This long fibre that carries impulses away from the cell body is the axon. Exam Tip: Axon and away both start with the letter a.

mcq.questionText: The junction where one neurone meets another and impulses pass between them is called a:
mcq.explanation: This junction between two neurones is a synapse. Exam Tip: At a synapse, impulses cross the gap using chemical messengers.

mcq.questionText: A quick, automatic response to a stimulus that does not involve conscious thought is called a:
mcq.explanation: This fast, involuntary response is a reflex action. Exam Tip: Pulling your hand away from something hot is a classic example of a reflex action.

mcq.questionText: The pathway followed by a nerve impulse during a reflex action, from receptor to effector, is called the:
mcq.explanation: This complete pathway from receptor to effector is the reflex arc. Exam Tip: The reflex arc order is receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone, motor neurone, then effector.

mcq.questionText: The part of the eye that is sensitive to light and forms the image is the:
mcq.explanation: The retina is the light-sensitive layer that forms the image. Exam Tip: Think of the retina as the image-forming layer, like camera film.

mcq.questionText: The coloured part of the eye that controls the size of the pupil, regulating light entry, is the:
mcq.explanation: This coloured structure that controls pupil size is the iris. Exam Tip: The iris widens the pupil in dim light and narrows it in bright light.

mcq.questionText: The gland that produces insulin, a hormone that controls blood sugar level, is the:
mcq.explanation: The pancreas produces insulin, the hormone that controls blood sugar level. Exam Tip: The pancreas works as both a digestive gland and an endocrine gland.

mcq.questionText: The gland known as the "master gland" because it controls the activity of other endocrine glands is the:
mcq.explanation: This gland that controls other endocrine glands is the pituitary gland. Exam Tip: The pituitary gland regulates the activity of many other glands in the body.

mcq.questionText: The hormone released by the adrenal glands during times of fear or stress, preparing the body for "fight or flight", is:
mcq.explanation: Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands during stress. Exam Tip: Adrenaline increases heart rate, breathing rate and blood flow to the muscles.

fib.questionText: The directional growth response of a plant to a stimulus is called __________.
fib.explanation: This directional growth response of a plant to a stimulus is called tropism. Exam Tip: Named by stimulus: photo-, geo-, hydro-, thigmo-tropism.

fib.questionText: Growth of a shoot towards light is called positive __________.
fib.explanation: Growth of a shoot towards light is positive phototropism. Exam Tip: Positive phototropism = towards light (shoots).

fib.questionText: The basic functional unit of the nervous system is the __________.
fib.explanation: The basic functional unit of the nervous system is the neurone. Exam Tip: Neurones carry electrical impulses throughout the body.

fib.questionText: The junction between two neurones where impulses pass across is called a __________.
fib.explanation: This junction between two neurones is called a synapse. Exam Tip: Chemical messengers cross the synapse gap.

fib.questionText: A fast, automatic, involuntary response to a stimulus is called a __________ action.
fib.explanation: This fast, involuntary response is called a reflex action. Exam Tip: Reflexes happen without conscious thought.

fib.questionText: The complete nerve pathway used in a reflex action is called the reflex __________.
fib.explanation: This complete nerve pathway used in a reflex action is called the reflex arc. Exam Tip: Reflex arc: receptor -> sensory neurone -> relay -> motor neurone -> effector.

fib.questionText: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye where images are formed is the __________.
fib.explanation: This light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye is the retina. Exam Tip: The retina works like camera film.

fib.questionText: The hormone produced by the pancreas that lowers blood sugar level is called __________.
fib.explanation: This hormone produced by the pancreas that lowers blood sugar level is insulin. Exam Tip: Lack of insulin causes diabetes.

fib.questionText: The gland called the "master gland" of the endocrine system is the __________ gland.
fib.explanation: This gland called the master gland is the pituitary gland. Exam Tip: Controls thyroid, adrenal, and reproductive glands.

fib.questionText: The hormone released during stress that prepares the body for "fight or flight" is __________.
fib.explanation: This hormone released during stress that prepares the body for fight or flight is adrenaline. Exam Tip: Adrenaline comes from the adrenal glands.

tf.questionText: Tropism is the directional growth response of a plant to a stimulus.
tf.explanation: This statement is correct because tropism is defined as the directional growth response of a plant to a stimulus. Exam Tip: Tropisms can be positive (towards) or negative (away).

tf.questionText: Plant roots show negative geotropism, growing away from gravity.
tf.explanation: This statement is false because roots grow towards gravity, showing positive geotropism, not negative. Exam Tip: Roots show positive geotropism (down).

tf.questionText: The axon of a neurone carries impulses away from the cell body.
tf.explanation: This statement is correct because the axon is the fibre that carries impulses away from the cell body. Exam Tip: Axon = away; dendrite = towards.

tf.questionText: A synapse is the part of a neurone that stores nerve impulses permanently.
tf.explanation: This statement is false because a synapse only transmits impulses between neurones; nothing is stored there. Exam Tip: Synapses transmit impulses; nothing is stored there.

tf.questionText: A reflex action occurs quickly and does not require conscious thought.
tf.explanation: This statement is correct because reflex actions are fast and involuntary. Exam Tip: Speed protects the body from harm.

tf.questionText: The retina of the eye controls the amount of light entering by changing pupil size.
tf.explanation: This statement is false because the iris controls pupil size, while the retina forms the image. Exam Tip: The iris controls pupil size; retina forms the image.

tf.questionText: The pancreas produces insulin, which helps control blood sugar level.
tf.explanation: This statement is correct because the pancreas produces insulin, which lowers blood sugar level. Exam Tip: Insufficient insulin leads to diabetes.

tf.questionText: The pituitary gland is called the "master gland" because it controls other endocrine glands.
tf.explanation: This statement is correct because the pituitary gland controls the activity of other endocrine glands. Exam Tip: Located at the base of the brain.

tf.questionText: Adrenaline slows down the heart rate during stress.
tf.explanation: This statement is false because adrenaline increases the heart rate during stress, preparing the body for fight or flight. Exam Tip: Adrenaline INCREASES heart rate - fight or flight.

tf.questionText: The reflex arc pathway includes a receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone, motor neurone and effector.
tf.explanation: This statement is correct because this is the standard order of structures in a reflex arc. Exam Tip: This order is heavily tested.

summary.correctAnswer: The directional growth response of a plant to a stimulus, which can be positive (towards) or negative (away).
summary.explanation: Tropisms are named according to the stimulus involved. Exam Tip: Remember photo-(light), geo-(gravity), hydro-(water), thigmo-(touch).

summary.correctAnswer: The growth response of a plant towards or away from light; shoots show positive phototropism and roots show negative phototropism.
summary.explanation: Shoots bend towards light to maximise photosynthesis. Exam Tip: Positive phototropism means growth towards light.

summary.correctAnswer: The growth response of a plant towards or away from gravity; roots show positive geotropism and shoots show negative geotropism.
summary.explanation: Roots grow downward into the soil for anchorage and water. Exam Tip: Positive geotropism means growth towards gravity, that is, downward.

summary.correctAnswer: The dendrite receives impulses and carries them towards the cell body; the axon is the long fibre that carries impulses away from the cell body.
summary.explanation: Together, dendrites and axons allow a neurone to receive and transmit nerve impulses. Exam Tip: Dendrite is towards the cell body; axon is away from it.

summary.correctAnswer: The junction between two neurones where nerve impulses pass across using chemical messengers.
summary.explanation: No impulse is stored at a synapse; it only allows transmission between neurones. Exam Tip: Chemical messengers cross the gap at a synapse.

summary.correctAnswer: The complete nerve pathway of a reflex action: receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone, motor neurone, and effector.
summary.explanation: The reflex arc bypasses conscious brain processing, making the response very fast. Exam Tip: Memorise the order: receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone, motor neurone, effector.

summary.correctAnswer: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye that forms the image; the iris is the coloured part that controls the size of the pupil to regulate light entry.
summary.explanation: The retina works like camera film while the iris acts like a shutter. Exam Tip: Retina forms the image; iris controls pupil size.

summary.correctAnswer: The pancreas is the gland that produces insulin, a hormone that lowers blood sugar level by helping cells absorb glucose.
summary.explanation: The pancreas is both a digestive and an endocrine gland. Exam Tip: A lack of insulin, or an ineffective response to it, causes diabetes.

summary.correctAnswer: The endocrine gland known as the "master gland" because it controls the activity of other endocrine glands such as the thyroid and adrenal glands.
summary.explanation: It is located at the base of the brain. Exam Tip: The pituitary gland regulates many other glands in the body.

summary.correctAnswer: The hormone released by the adrenal glands during fear or stress, preparing the body for "fight or flight" by increasing heart rate, breathing rate, and blood flow to the muscles.
summary.explanation: Adrenaline is a fast-acting hormone for emergency response. Exam Tip: Adrenaline increases heart rate; it does not slow it down.

hoq.questionText: A potted plant on a windowsill with light from one side: the shoot bends towards the light, while the roots grow further down and away from the light. Explain this using tropisms.

options.text: Both are examples of geotropism only
The shoot shows positive phototropism (grows towards light) and the root shows positive geotropism (grows towards gravity, downward, away from light)
The shoot shows negative phototropism; the root shows negative geotropism

hoq.explanation: The shoot bends towards light because it shows positive phototropism, while the root grows down into the soil towards gravity, showing positive geotropism. Exam Tip: Shoots and roots respond oppositely to the same stimuli.

hoq.questionText: A doctor taps below a patient's kneecap and the leg kicks forward without conscious effort. Describe the pathway involved and explain why the response is so fast.

options.text: The impulse travels to the brain for conscious decision-making, which takes time

The impulse follows a reflex arc (receptor -> sensory neurone -> relay neurone in the spinal cord -> motor neurone -> effector muscle), bypassing conscious brain processing, making the response very fast
The impulse travels only through the pituitary gland

hoq.explanation: The impulse travels via a reflex arc through the spinal cord without going to the brain first, making the response fast. Exam Tip: The knee-jerk is the standard textbook example of a spinal reflex arc.

hoq.questionText: A diabetic student has very high blood sugar after meals, while a healthy classmate's blood sugar returns to normal quickly. Explain this difference using the pancreas and insulin.

options.text: The diabetic student's pancreas produces too much insulin

The diabetic student's pancreas produces too little insulin (or the body cannot respond to it properly), so glucose is not taken up by cells efficiently and blood sugar remains high; the healthy classmate's pancreas releases enough insulin to lower blood sugar after eating
Insulin has no role in blood sugar control
Blood sugar level is unrelated to the pancreas

hoq.explanation: A healthy pancreas releases enough insulin to help cells absorb glucose after a meal, but a diabetic student's pancreas produces too little insulin or the body responds to it poorly, so blood sugar stays high. Exam Tip: Insulin LOWERS blood sugar by helping cells absorb glucose.
